findings.title: Recovery-code metadata (hash, label, timestamp) is dropped when delegating to a UserStorageProvider
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds a plain UserCredentialModel containing only the raw, unhashed JSON list of generated codes (recoveryCodesJson) and passes that to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The already-built RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel passed into the method (which contains the hashed codes, the user-chosen label and the generation timestamp) is only used on the local-storage fallback path and is discarded whenever a UserStorageProvider accepts the update. Any UserStorageProvider implementation therefore receives raw codes and no label/timestamp, and must re-implement hashing and reconstruct metadata itself (or lose it entirely, as the shipped reference implementation does). This is a real loss of functionality/metadata for the new 'recovery codes in user storage' feature, not just a theoretical concern, since the included test provider demonstrates exactly this loss.

findings.title: Recovery codes are persisted unhashed in the reference UserStorageProvider implementation
findings.body: In updateCredential(), the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE branch stores input.getChallengeResponse() (the raw, unhashed JSON array of generated recovery codes) directly as credentialData with no hashing, unlike how the local DB-backed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider stores codes (hashed). This is the provider shipped as the reference/test implementation for the new 'store recovery codes in user storage' feature, and it stores backup authentication codes in cleartext, which is an insecure pattern that could be copied by real implementers of UserStorageProvider.

findings.title: Recovery codes validated through the user-storage provider are never marked as consumed, allowing infinite reuse
findings.body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never removes/marks the matched code as used, nor persists any updated state back to `myUser.recoveryCodes`. Recovery/backup codes are meant to be single-use; with this implementation the exact same code can be used to authenticate an unlimited number of times when the credential is stored via this UserStorageProvider, defeating the core security property of recovery codes. Because the integration test (testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin) only logs in once, this defect is not caught by the new tests.

findings.title: getCredentials() can throw NullPointerException when the user is unknown to this storage
findings.body: getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel) calls `getMyUser(user)` and then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes`/`myUser.otp` without checking `myUser != null`. Every other method in this class that uses getMyUser() (getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isConfiguredFor) explicitly guards against a null result, but this new method does not, so a call for a user not present in the backing map will throw an NPE instead of returning an empty stream.

findings.title: New recovery-codes-in-user-storage test does not cover code consumption, reuse prevention, or credential removal
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only sets up recovery codes in the custom user storage and performs a single successful login with one code. It never verifies that a used code cannot be reused, that the credential is removed/required action re-added once all codes are consumed (mirroring RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator's allCodesUsed()/removeStoredCredentialById logic), or that disabling/removing the credential works for the federated case (as is done for OTP in testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin and testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage). As a result, the actual data-integrity bug in the shipped BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() (codes never consumed) goes undetected.

findings.title: Hard-coded credential provider id instead of the existing constant
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() looks up the provider with the literal string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, which was previously referenced directly (and imported) in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction before this change removed that import. Using a magic string loses compile-time safety: if the provider id ever changes, this call will silently fail at runtime (NPE from session.getProvider returning null) instead of failing to compile.

findings.title: New getCredentials() override also changes existing OTP credential exposure, outside the scope of the recovery-codes feature
findings.body: To support the new feature, updateCredential() now assigns a real generated id to the OTP CredentialModel (newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())), and the newly added getCredentials() override unconditionally includes myUser.getOtp() whenever an OTP credential exists. Previously this provider did not implement getCredentials(), so OTP credentials were not exposed through the generic federated-credential discovery path at all. This is a behavior change for OTP handling in this provider that is incidental to the recovery-codes feature and is not covered by any new or existing test specifically validating that OTP account-management flows (e.g. listing/deleting OTP credentials via account REST) still behave the same with this newly real, generated credential id.
